subject: ventures/einvoice-preflight
professional: an e-invoicing compliance consultant who certifies ERP output against EN 16931, Peppol BIS 3.0 and XRechnung validators. What they check first: does the built-in pre-screen agree with the official CEN Schematron on BR-CO-10/14/15/16/17 to the cent, on ordinary and on large amounts? Does the official route give the same verdicts as Saxon on the CEN XSLT? Are the identifier check digits the published algorithms? Does a 'repair' ever make a valid invoice invalid?

evidence.correctness: Scored independently, against sources the author did not write. Fourth audit; about 61 commits under the subject since 2026-11-09 (Peppol COMMON id rules, Self-Billing, BIS 3.1.0 preview, French BR-FR/CDAR/Flux 10, INV-065, the rounding change in #16129). (1) Official route vs CEN: I generated 600 random UBL invoices (scratchpad gen.py, seed 20261119: 1-4 lines, 15 VAT rates, half-cent ties, amounts of 1e10 to 1e12, and planted BR-CO-15/16/17 faults). I ran CEN's own EN16931-UBL-validation.xslt (Schematron 1.3.17, fetched from ConnectingEurope/eInvoicing-EN16931) under SaxonC-HE (saxonche) and compared its fatal BR-* ids with the tool's schematron:true route (plain rules on fontoxpath, in a scratch copy with slimdom/fontoxpath installed): 600 of 600 identical. 9 shipped UBL examples: 9 of 9 identical. (2) Hand recompute of examples/ubl-invoice-with-defects.xml: 200x19% = 38.00 (INV-038 says 38), 350 + 46.60 = 396.60 (INV-017), 380 - 98.50 = 281.50 (INV-029). All correct. (3) The 2026-11-07 half-cent tie defect is fixed: roundHalfUpToCents(0.285) = 0.29, 1.005 = 1.01, 2.675 = 2.68, -0.285 = -0.29. All 55 tie invoices agree with CEN. (4) But that fix (#16129, toPrecision(12)) truncates any amount whose value in cents has more than 12 significant digits. On a correct IDR invoice (line 12,345,678,901.23 at 11%, tax 1,358,024,679.14, gross 13,703,703,580.37) CEN reports nothing and the Python CLI reports nothing (Decimal). The built-in JS route (page, API, schematron-cli) reports INV-017 'Set gross total to 13703703580.30', INV-018 and INV-038 'Set tax to 1358024679.13'. repairUbl rewrites the file to taxable 12345678901.20 and gross 13703703580.30, and CEN then rejects the repaired file (BR-CO-10, BR-CO-15). In the 600-file run: 0 false INV-017/029/038 on the 195 ordinary correct files, but 51 false findings across the 61 large-amount files. (5) VAT check digits vs python-stdnum 2.2 on 12,000 random numbers in 20 countries (scratchpad vatgen.py seed 1119): 11,944 agree. The 56 differences are the README's documented deliberate ones: DE leading 0 accepted, where stdnum rejects; EE not starting with 1 rejected. NO and CH agree 600/600. (6) IBAN by ISO 13616 mod 97 (GB82WEST..., DE89..., NO93..., BE71..., two one-digit typos) and Leitweg-ID by ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 (04011000-12345-03, 991-01234-38, two typos): every verdict right. (7) Mandate dates: DE 1 Jan 2025 receive, 1 Jan 2027 issue above EUR 800,000, 1 Jan 2028 all. Checked against the BMF FAQ fetched today ('Bei einem Vorjahresumsatz ... bis 800.000 Euro verlängert sich diese Frist noch bis zum Ablauf des Jahres 2027'). PL 1 Feb 2026, 1 Apr 2026, 1 Jan 2027; FR 1 Sep 2026 and 1 Sep 2027; BE 1 Jan 2026; HR 1 Jan 2026: these match the statutes as I know them (podatki.gov.pl renders by JS and impots.gouv.fr was in maintenance, so those are not re-read today). Score 3, not 2: on ordinary amounts both routes are right and the official route is exact. The wrong numbers start at amounts of 10^10 with sub-unit digits, which excludes almost every EUR invoice but not IDR. Recorded as a high defect.
evidence.completeness: Claims exercised: UBL/CII/JSON readers (report.mjs, the module the page imports), the official EN 16931 route (schematron:true), repair-ubl, VAT/IBAN/BIC/Leitweg checks, the Python CLI on the same examples, the served copy (served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin), and mandate-dates.json (the source of ~90 country pages and the ICS). All worked end to end. The documented limits still hold: the Python CLI lacks profiles, PDF envelope checks and NO/CH VAT, and veraPDF is unrun. No stubs or TODOs met. The page was not loaded in a browser this round; the page's own module was run under Node.
evidence.verification: `node --test '*.test.mjs'` in the subject: 2307 tests, 2168 pass, 0 fail, 139 skipped, 8.9 s. 100+ of the skips need slimdom/fontoxpath for the official route. In a scratch copy with `npm i --no-save slimdom fontoxpath`: 2291 pass, 0 fail, 16 skipped. CI (.github/workflows/einvoice-preflight-ci.yml:63) runs plain `node --test` without them, so the official-route tests never run in CI. Python: `PYTHONPATH=src pytest -q tests`: 440 passed, 263 subtests. Five mutations, using quality_mutate.py. Caught: the tie-rounding fix reverted (2 tests fail); INV-029 given a 1-cent tolerance; INV-038 given a 1-cent tolerance. Survived the full suite: BG EGN remainder-10 mapped to 1, and CZ 10-digit `% 10` dropped. These are the same two survivors the 2026-11-09 audit reported, still with no remainder-10 test. No test has an amount of 1e10 or more, which is how the toPrecision regression got in.
evidence.craft: Read checks.mjs:1-60,110-130,355-372, breakdown.mjs:1-130, linenet.mjs:11-15, adjustment.mjs:11-15, vat.mjs:85-230,1013-1029, repair-ubl.mjs:40-60, report.mjs exports, the CI workflow, src/einvoice_preflight/vat.py. Positives: compiled official rule sets that match Saxon, careful comments citing the rule each check implements, a Python port that uses Decimal. Defects: the same rounding idiom is pasted in seven places (checks, breakdown, adjustment, linenet, creditlink, cfdi, repair-ubl x2) instead of one integer-cents or decimal-string helper, so one shared defect sits in all seven. The README has grown from 116 KB to 393 KB of dated run log. The 2026-11-09 defects were not marked fixed or recorded in fix_prs, and two of them are untouched.
evidence.claims: Not backed: checks.mjs:1-3 says it mirrors checks.py 'so the browser page and the CLI report the same rule IDs, messages, and cent-rounded arithmetic'. index.html:188 says 'The same local rules as the CLI' and :211 'The same checks run from python3 -m einvoice_preflight'. All three are false. The IDR invoice gives 3 findings in JS and 0 in Python. NO/CH VAT, profiles and the PDF checks are JS only. The messages differ ('Set tax to 38' in JS, '38.00' in Python). This is the fourth audit to report it. Backed: disclaimer (index.html:333), nothing uploaded (no fetch in report path; only licence key sent, as stated), VENTURE.yaml stage prototype with untested hypotheses, the llms.txt claim of the same rule ids as SaxonC (my own 609/609 agrees), the README's stdnum differential claims (reproduced), served llms.txt/sitemap clean. README line 1189 calls INV-005 'a style note', but it is a blocking error (exit 1, status fail).
evidence.fitness: The integrator's job: drop the ERP's UBL, read the rule ids and fixes, tick the official box for the CEN/Peppol/XRechnung sets, then repair arithmetic. For a European ERP this works, and the official route is as good as running the CEN XSLT. Gaps they would hit: (a) the default built-in route flags INV-038/INV-018 for a tax 0.01 off the exact figure (line-level rounding), which the official validator accepts. In my run 80/80 such invoices were flagged and CEN passed all of them; nothing explains this. (b) Every EN 16931 invoice whose buyer has no identifier fails INV-005, although BT-46 is optional (600/600 of my generated files). (c) Indonesian-scale amounts (10^10 IDR with sen) get wrong fixes, and the repair corrupts them. Verdict: usable as a pre-screen by someone who knows these quirks.
evidence.domain: Compared against the CEN EN 16931 Schematron 1.3.17 (ConnectingEurope) and the business-rule text. Matches: BR-CO-10/14/15/16 arithmetic, BR-61, BR-S-09, BR-CL-01 on the official route (609/609 against Saxon). Identifier algorithms (ISO 13616, ISO 7064 MOD 97-10, stdnum's national rules) are right. The mandate dates match the BMF and the statutes. Departures on the built-in route: BR-CO-17 is enforced to the exact cent as a blocking error, where CEN allows a difference under one unit; INV-005 requires a buyer id EN 16931 does not; and amounts at or above 10^10 are rounded at the 13th significant digit, which no decimal arithmetic allows. A consultant would sign off the official route and treat the built-in one as an advisory lint.

defects.what: The tie-rounding fix (#16129) rounds value*100 to 12 significant digits, so any amount of 10^10 or more with sub-unit digits is truncated before it is compared. On a correct IDR invoice (line 12,345,678,901.23 at 11%), which CEN and the Python CLI both pass, the page/API report INV-017 'Set gross total to 13703703580.30' (correct .37) and INV-018/INV-038 'Set tax to 1358024679.13' (correct .14). repairUbl then rewrites the valid file into one CEN rejects (BR-CO-10, BR-CO-15). 51 false findings on 61 large-amount files. No test uses an amount of 1e10 or more.
defects.where: ventures/einvoice-preflight/checks.mjs:30 (same idiom at breakdown.mjs:17, adjustment.mjs:14, linenet.mjs:14, creditlink.mjs:36, repair-ubl.mjs:43,56)

defects.what: Still open from 2026-11-07 (fourth audit): the checks.mjs header claims the page and CLI give the same rule IDs, messages and cent-rounded arithmetic, and the page says 'The same local rules as the CLI' and 'The same checks run from python3 -m einvoice_preflight'. All false: the large-amount findings are JS only, NO/CH VAT, profiles and PDF checks are JS only, and the fix texts differ ('38' vs '38.00').

BR-CO-17 is enforced to the exact cent as a blocking INV-038 (and INV-018), where CEN's Schematron accepts a subtotal within one unit of taxable x rate. An invoice whose ERP rounds per line (tax 0.01 off) fails the pre-screen but passes the official validator: 151/151 such files in the differential. The stricter reading is not explained on the page or in the README, and it is not a warning.
Still open from 2026-11-09: no test has a remainder-10 number, so mapping the BG EGN remainder 10 to 1, or dropping the CZ 10-digit `% 10`, passes all 2307 tests (both mutants survived again).

CI runs `node --test` without slimdom/fontoxpath, so the 139 tests of the official EN 16931/Peppol/XRechnung/BR-FR route the page advertises are skipped on every PR. They pass when installed (2291 pass, 16 skip).

INV-005 fails every UBL/CII invoice whose buyer has a name but no identifier (BT-46/47/48/49 are all optional in EN 16931; CEN passes them). It is reported as a blocking error with exit 1, while README:1189 calls it 'a style note'.
Still open from 2026-11-08: Norway and Switzerland VAT check digits (#14052) are not in the Python port.
The rounding idiom is copy-pasted in seven places instead of one integer-cents/decimal helper, so the large-amount defect is in all of them. README.md is now a 393 KB run log (116 KB on 2026-11-09).

verdict: Fourth audit. The official route is now excellent. On 600 randomly generated UBL invoices and 9 shipped examples, its EN 16931 verdicts matched CEN's own Schematron 1.3.17 XSLT run under SaxonC-HE on all 609 files. VAT check digits agree with python-stdnum on 11,944 of 12,000 numbers, and the 56 differences are documented. IBAN, Leitweg and the German mandate dates (against the BMF FAQ) are right. The 2026-11-07 half-cent tie defect is fixed. But the fix rounds at 12 significant digits, so a correct invoice of 10^10 or more (realistic in IDR) draws wrong fixes on the page and API, and the UBL repair turns it into a file CEN rejects. The built-in route is also stricter than EN 16931 in two undocumented ways (BR-CO-17 to the exact cent, a buyer id required). The JS/Python parity claim is false for the fourth audit running. CI skips the 139 official-route tests. The two remainder-10 mutants from 2026-11-09 still survive. Does not meet the bar: claims 2 and verification 2, with correctness 3. Scores are before any fix.
